reviews.title: Dell makes quality products. This one is great value for money.
reviews.comment:
Very happy with the color and text display quality of this VA panel and no fear of burn-in as this is not an OLED. But still deeper blacks than IPS Black Panels.
Was worried about excessive heat generation like in my old plasma TV, but it's minimal. Much better power/heat efficiency than Mini LED and OLED panels.
Have not tested it for gaming but from what I've read, it's great for casual gaming.
Excellent value for $ with the USB-C connection to laptop for a clutter-free desktop. Very happy with this purchase!
reviews.author: Lance H

reviews.title: Best monitor I ever owned
reviews.comment: This is by far the best monitor I have ever owned—perfect resolution and color accuracy. I spend 40+ hrs a week working on graphic design, and it is a pleasure to look at the screen. The drop-down USB ports are super handy to charge a cell phone or a wireless mouse. Definitely recommended!

reviews.title: OK Monitor with few ports and VESA mount design flaw
reviews.comment:
I want to be clear here: this is not a bad monitor. It fits my setup, does the job, looks alright. However, it has very few ports. My 8-year old other Dell 34in curved monitor has many more, so if you need more connections of any kind, be mindful that there is not a lot. Mine has HDMI, USB-C, USB-A and that's it. No DisplayPort etc. Also the color is not as good as my older one.
If you need to attach it to a stand with the VESA interface, be aware that the place where the VESA bracket goes in is kind of sunk-in, by around 1/4 of an inch. That made it not possible to lift it up and slot it into place - instead, I had to mount the entire bracket assembly to it. Not a big deal, it works, it is just a bit annoying. You could fix that by adding small spacers instead, but I did not have anything around.
I also noticed that it is thicker and heavier than my older monitor. In the picture, the top monitor is the new one (this product), and the old one is the lower. Yes, it was cheaper, and it has 120Hz, I appreciate that, but honestly, there are many monitors of this kind out there that are at least 100 USD cheaper. I went for Dell because I already own a Dell monitor and I made good experience with it.
In summary, it does what I need it to do: provide more screen space. I am not a gamer, so I cannot comment on gaming performance. If I did not already have a Dell monitor, I would have probably bought 2 monitors from a different brand, mostly for cost reasons.
